items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Green, William and myself... were going from place to place doing our numbers

ctx.x: A very well known story in Ohio about the Whispering Serenaders is that they were engaged to work in big white exclusive hotels in different cities in Ohio, but they were also engaged to work in a white hotel somewhere down South. After being there for a while, they were asked to play for a party one night after work. This party was outside of the town at a private house, so some men were waiting for them in cars to take them and the instruments to this party. After having driven a few miles out of town, the cars…

A pianist by the name of Green came to Cincinnati and I met him along with a young fellow named William who played drums. Green was one of those pianists that played by ear and only in one key. There were at this time a couple of other young pianists around town who played by ear and were very popular. One was named Hershal Brown. He could play in any key although he could not read music. He played in an orchestra and he really could play fine.

But getting back to Green and William, I started going to different parties with them and playing a few numbers I had learned. I don't remember getting paid from these parties, but on Christmas night, Green, William and myself, I was known as Johnson, were going from place to place doing our numbers and drinking egg-nog. Many people gave open house parties on Christmas and New Year's and egg-nog was flowing that night like the water running over Niagara Falls.
